  --label security,priority/P3 --milestone "v1.2 Week 8 — spikes, decisions & cycle close" \
  --body "## Summary
\`request_otp\` (\`backend/app/api/v1/auth_otp.py:79-104\`) pads responses to \`auth_otp_request_min_seconds\` (default 1.0s), but that is a **minimum**, not a maximum. The eligible branch runs \`is_signup_eligible\` → per-email quota → DB writes → a **synchronous** \`mailer.send_code()\` (real SMTP round-trip) *before* the floor is applied; ineligible/throttled branches return fast and are padded to the same floor.

When a real relay (e.g. SES) pushes the eligible path's own work past ~1s, an allow-listed address produces a measurably longer tail than a non-member — revealing which addresses are workspace members. The code comment (\"Only a real mail-transport failure differs\") is optimistic: a slow-but-successful send also differs.

## Impact / severity
Low and deployment-dependent (floor vs. relay latency); Mailpit-local won't exhibit it. Membership enumeration only, not credential compromise.

## Fix
Send mail out-of-band (queue) so the response time is independent of transport latency, or measure-and-cap the send inside the floored region.

Found in a full-codebase QA auth surface audit (surface otherwise verified clean — no blocker/major)."

content.text:
All 12 issues filed (#1724–#1735). Here's the complete QA report.

## Verdict
The product is in strong shape — no crash-class blocker in shipped code, and the core auth/secrets/rate-limit and MCP surfaces are genuinely well-disciplined. But I found **12 real gaps that would otherwise have reached users**, two of them significant. I scanned the whole codebase (not just recent commits): the undeployed merged delta, the long-standing core surfaces, the entire 47-tool MCP surface, driver boundaries, and every published claim (docs site + marketing + README + in-app text) against the code — cross-checked with live probes on both clouds and full-path testing on the local stack.

## Issues filed

**P1**
- **[#1724]** `get_notification_config` (MCP) reports *"nobody gets the email alert"* when `EMAIL_FROM` is unset — but `EmailPublisher` falls back to `sender = username`, so alerts **are** delivered. The exact "who gets told → nobody" false answer this tool exists to prevent. Verified against `email.py:239/246` vs `server.py:1491`.
- **[#1725]** Compliance/security docs (`security.md`, `sub-processors.md`, `dpia-input-sheet.md`) state the outbound-LLM data-transfer vector is **"not built / Never"** — it's shipped and deployed to both clouds. A materially false GDPR Chapter V disclosure; the runtime posture endpoint already says `llm_intelligence: live`.

**P2**
- **[#1726]** Reaper threshold mis-calibration: `llm_invoke` and `run_suite` share one Celery queue (no `task_routes`), so a `run_suite` backlog lets the pending-reaper **false-kill** a still-queued invocation with a false "dispatch lost" reason (message intact in broker). Plus the 10-min running threshold ignores checksuggest's live warehouse-profiling leg.
- **[#1727]** Check-suggestions discards the `rejected` reasons in the **all-rejected** case — exactly where the docstring tells users to look for "why".
- **[#1728]** dbt colon-collision fail-closed guard (#1714) applied only in `incident_evidence`, not the forward correlators (`list_pipeline_runs`, `Results.tsx`).
- **[#1733]** Docs staleness sweep — DMF engine live+in-editor but docs say "planned"; per-suite Slack/email undocumented; "46 tools" vs 47; UC documented as DataFrame-bound when pushdown is default; stale in-app Settings strings.

**P3**
- **[#1729]** `jsonsafe` sanitizes dict values but not keys → latent JSONB crash on a bytes/Decimal key.
- **[#1730]** No test asserts either reaper's beat entry exists — a dropped schedule entry silently disables the silent-death compensator.
- **[#1731]** OTP request enumeration timing side-channel (floor is a minimum; synchronous SMTP send happens before it).
- **[#1732]** `update_connection` accepts `secret=""` at the service layer — blank-credential/redirect-guard bypass rests on a single API-model check.
- **[#1734]** Check-suggestion prompt unbounded by column count.
- **[#1735]** UI "Triggered by" shows raw `manual:<uuid>`.

## Verified working (live, not assumed)
Both clouds' gates + 6/6 security headers + CSP; per-suite scoping on prod (member sees exactly 1 suite); OTP sign-in (enumeration-safe); LLM config → live test (Ollama) → dispatch → worker → poll → honest fail-soft on an unreachable warehouse; the reaper **live-reaps** a stuck row correctly; Admin surfaces render honestly (em-dash for no-data, workspace-true asset health, `#1401` destination-move guard, audit of the config change, honest data-residency table). The five agents independently confirmed the reap-race fix is complete, authz/rate-limit/output-trust are clean, the #1624 UC pushdown is well-evidenced, and MCP tool-count/gate declarations have zero drift.

## Assumptions & decisions I made (and why)
- **"Merged ≠ deployed ≠ works"** (the repo's own lesson) — so I verified prod by HTTP, confirmed the undeployed #1513 route is 404 on prod, and rebuilt the crash-looping local image (stale, missing `anthropic`) rather than trusting `docker ps`.
- **Re-verified every agent finding myself** before filing — the beat-test claim I *narrowed* (a typo *is* caught; only a dropped entry isn't); the email and queue findings I confirmed at the exact source lines.
- **Local DB is a perf-test snapshot**, not the prod mirror — its only connection (UC) is unreachable, so the LLM *success* path could only reach the honest fail-soft locally; the full dispatch/persist plumbing was exercised. This is the main gap in this pass, along with no live multi-worker reproduction of the queue false-kill and no AWS authenticated-write probe (no non-interactive Cognito bearer).
- Kept to ~5 concurrent agents on disjoint surfaces (credit budget); consolidated 13 doc divergences into one tracked issue rather than 13 tickets; secrets fetched inline, never printed.

One note: I left the local stack's LLM provider pointed at Ollama (a harmless local-only config change I made to test the path).

This is a race against queue depth, so a clean repro means forcing the backlog:
1. Set \`LLM_INVOCATION_PENDING_THRESHOLD_MINUTES=1\` (shrinks the window so you don't have to wait 15 min).
2. Enqueue several long \`run_suite\` tasks (the large UC perf suites take minutes each) to saturate the single worker's prefork slots.
3. Immediately \`POST /llm/sql_generation\` (or \`/check_suggestions\`) so its message queues *behind* the runs.
4. Wait past the pending threshold while the runs still occupy the worker.

Observed: the invocation is reaped to \`failed\` (\"the dispatch was likely lost before a worker claimed it\") **while its message is still in the broker**; when a worker slot frees, \`execute_invocation\`'s claim finds \`status='failed'\` and returns \`skipped\` → the request is permanently dead with a false cause.

Confirmed by inspection (no repro needed for the mechanism): \`celery_app.py\` \`conf.update\` has no \`task_routes\`/\`task_default_queue\`, and \`run_dispatch.py:43,48\` sends both task types to the one default queue.
Part B (running false-reap) is likewise latency-dependent — reproduce by pointing checksuggest at a cold/suspended warehouse with a wide table and a slow provider so the \`running\` phase exceeds 10 min."

gh issue comment 1731 --repo TheurgicDuke771/DataQ --body "## How to observe (statistical — deployment-dependent, not a single-shot repro)
Requires a real SMTP relay whose send latency can exceed the 1.0s floor (Mailpit-local will NOT exhibit it):
1. Configure a live relay (e.g. SES) for OTP.
2. Time \`POST /api/v1/auth/otp/request\` for (a) an allow-listed/member address vs (b) a non-member address, N≥100 samples each.
3. Observed: (a)'s tail exceeds (b)'s whenever the synchronous \`mailer.send_code()\` pushes the eligible path past the floor — the floor pads (b) up to ~1.0s but cannot pad (a) *down*. The delta reveals membership.

The mechanism is confirmed by inspection: the floor (\`_hold_until_floor\`) is a minimum applied *after* the eligible branch's synchronous SMTP send (\`auth_otp.py:79-104\`, \`otp_service.py:230-272\`). Severity is low/deployment-dependent, hence P3."

It is equally wrong for generic-OIDC (any issuer) and email-OTP deployments (where the right hint is a session cookie or PAT).

- ADR 0010/0026 cloud-neutrality: no Azure identity assumptions should leak into surface behavior; this is user-facing proof of the opposite.
- Actionability: the message steers a Cognito/OTP user toward a credential type that cannot work on their deployment.

## Fix
Make the message auth-mode-aware (the auth ladder already knows its active mode) or neutral: \"Not authenticated: a valid sign-in token, session, or DataQ API key (dq_live_…) is required.\"
